To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
convex relaxations of clustering problems can be very powerful tools for exact recovery, and that they can be used to provide a theoretical understanding of the limitations of common heuristics.

(a) convex relaxations can be used to exactly recover the clusters in the point cloud clustering problems under a wide variety of assumptions over the input; and (b) in contrast, common heuristic algorithms such as Lloyd's k-means algorithm and k-means++ can fail to recover the clusters even under very mild separation conditions.

(1) the k-median LP relaxation is exact for any pairwise cluster separation ε>0, (2) the k-means relaxation is not exact for any pairwise separation δ < 4, (3) the k-meas relaxation with PSD constraints is exact for pairwise separation δ > min{4, 2 + √2, 2 + 2 /m}, and (4) k-means++ is not exact for δ < 2+√k.
